gap_matrix.subtopic: SoD authorization/recordkeeping/reconciliation separation
gap_matrix.ec_quality: Statement-level only. Names SoD concept correctly but lacks COSO reference, business interpretation, exam-trap guidance.
gap_matrix.choices_summary: A=SoD (correct), B=cost-benefit analysis, C=management override, D=risk acceptance. All are genuine COSO/control concepts. D is weakest distractor.

gap_matrix.subtopic: Five-component framework recognition
gap_matrix.ec_quality: Exemplary. Names COSO explicitly, lists all five components, functions as self-contained mini-lesson.
gap_matrix.cc_note: Agent C (metadata) says D; Agent D (content) says A. DL-016 metadata-content shift. EW_CC slot correct in both cases.
gap_matrix.choices_summary: A=Six Sigma DMAIC, B=Balanced Scorecard, C=Theory of Constraints, D=COSO (correct). All distractors are prominent business frameworks — Bloom's Remember level.
certification_blockers: Distractor quality critically low (DQS 14) — DL-031 definition-match pattern

gap_matrix.subtopic: Pressure/Opportunity/Rationalization identification
gap_matrix.ec_quality: Bare definition only. Names three fraud triangle elements but no business interpretation, no organizational context, no exam-trap guidance.
gap_matrix.cc_note: Agent C (metadata) says C; Agent D (content) says B. DL-016 shift — content-block CC is B; only EW_D has text.
gap_matrix.choices_summary: A=Five Forces, B=Fraud Triangle, C=Balanced Scorecard, D=COSO ERM cube. Stem gives away answer with three elements listed. DL-031 definition-match. Only 1 of 3 non-CC slots has content.
certification_blockers: DL-031 definition-match pattern — should be Easy/1

gap_matrix.subtopic: Locked warehouse/badge access as preventive physical control
gap_matrix.ec_quality: Good. Explains physical safeguarding, custody control, and unauthorized access prevention. Missing explicit COSO component mapping.
gap_matrix.dl010_note: CRITICAL (S809.2 Agent B): EWB describes physical access but distractor B is about monthly bank rec. EWC describes compensating controls but distractor C is about quarterly audit review. Both EW texts are from entirely different question. All 3 distractor slots broken.
gap_matrix.choices_summary: A=entity-level control, B=detective control only, C=compensating control, D=physical control (correct). Good control-type discrimination.
certification_blockers: DL-010: EW_B and EW_C describe wrong items' distractors — learner sees unrelated feedback

gap_matrix.topic: Segregation of duties — vendor setup and payment
gap_matrix.subtopic: SoD vendor master file creation vs. payment approval
gap_matrix.ec_quality: Strong. Explains incompatible-duties conflict, identifies preventive authorization control. Clear business context. Missing explicit COSO reference.
gap_matrix.choices_summary: A=second employee approval + vendor-master review (correct), B=same employee does bank rec (makes problem worse), C=quarterly auditor review (detective-only), D=raise dollar threshold (counterproductive). Best quality seed in Pack C. Genuine CMA-style traps.

gap_matrix.topic: Preventive vs. detective — duplicate payment control
gap_matrix.subtopic: System-imposed duplicate-check before payment = preventive
gap_matrix.ec_quality: Good. Clearly distinguishes preventive from detective with specific mechanism. Practical business context. Missing COSO activity-level control taxonomy.
gap_matrix.choices_summary: A=weekly check register review (detective), B=AP system rejects duplicates before payment (correct, preventive), C=quarterly vendor statement rec (detective), D=monthly aging report review (detective). Core CMA preventive/detective distinction.

gap_matrix.topic: IT access control — terminated employee deprovisioning
gap_matrix.subtopic: Automated HR-triggered access revocation + recertification
gap_matrix.ec_quality: Good. Explains timing gap between termination and deprovisioning, purpose of recertification. Relevant to real-world IT control.
gap_matrix.choices_summary: A=accept risk since no actual harm, B=stronger password complexity (wrong control domain), C=automated deprovisioning + recertification (correct), D=read-only access instead of removal (half-measure). Highest DQS in pool (48). Realistic scenario detail ('18 days').

gap_matrix.topic: Application input control — sales order validation
gap_matrix.subtopic: Real-time field validation as preventive input control
gap_matrix.ec_quality: Strong. Identifies real-time field validation as application input control. Checks completeness/validity/reasonableness. Clear preventive vs. detective distinction.
gap_matrix.choices_summary: A=weekly exception reports (detective), B=month-end reconciliation (detective), C=manual supervisor approval (inefficient, may miss format errors), D=real-time field validation (correct). Good application-control question.

gap_matrix.subtopic: Dual signatures before check release = preventive authorization
gap_matrix.ec_quality: Good. Explains why dual signatures are preventive (timing: before cash leaves). Names control type as authorization. Missing explicit COSO reference.
gap_matrix.choices_summary: A=preventive control (correct), B=compensating control only, C=corrective control (after-the-fact), D=detective control. Tests core preventive/detective/corrective/compensating classification.

gap_matrix.subtopic: Independent bank rec as detective cash control
gap_matrix.ec_quality: Strong. Names bank rec as detective cash control. Explains independence rationale (outside cash handling/recording). Good real-world relevance.
gap_matrix.choices_summary: A=guarantees no bank fees (obviously wrong), B=removes need for management review, C=eliminates need to compare bank statements, D=ensures objective error detection (correct). Weak distractors — A and C are definitionally wrong. Correct answer is longest (length cueing).
certification_blockers: Distractor quality low — A and C are obviously wrong. Length cueing on correct answer.

gap_matrix.subtopic: Board-defined risk tolerance = risk appetite concept
gap_matrix.ec_quality: Definition-level. Correctly defines risk appetite but lacks business context, exam-trap guidance, or contrast with risk tolerance/capacity.
gap_matrix.cc_note: Agent C (metadata) says C; Agent D (content) says D. DL-016 shift.
gap_matrix.choices_summary: A=risk transfer, B=inherent risk, C=risk appetite (correct), D=control risk. DL-031 definition-match — stem directly defines 'risk appetite'. Two empty slots + EC definition-only.

gap_matrix.topic: IT general controls — logical access review
gap_matrix.subtopic: Periodic user access review as ITGC over logical access
gap_matrix.ec_quality: Good. Names IT general control and logical access categories. Explains least privilege principle. Solid instructional value.
gap_matrix.choices_summary: A=application control (embedded in transactions), B=budgetary control over IT spending, C=physical control over data center, D=IT general control over logical access (correct). Good ITGC vs. application control vs. physical control discrimination.

gap_matrix.subtopic: CEO-controller override as inherent limitation of internal control
gap_matrix.ec_quality: Strong. Uses scenario context (CEO instructing controller). Identifies as inherent limitation. Relevant and practical.
gap_matrix.choices_summary: A=management override (correct), B=SoD working as designed (clever/funny distractor), C=IT general control weakness, D=cost-benefit limitation. B is the best distractor in Pack C — but EW_B is empty.

gap_matrix.subtopic: Anonymous reporting channel = fraud detection and monitoring
gap_matrix.ec_quality: Good. Explains hotline role in fraud-risk monitoring and detection. Connects to information and communication. Honest qualifying language.
gap_matrix.choices_summary: A=encouraging detection/reporting (correct), B=guaranteeing no fraud ever occurs (absolute language trap), C=replacing code of conduct, D=eliminating need for external audit. B is absolute-language cue.

gap_matrix.subtopic: Owner/management review as compensating control when SoD not feasible
gap_matrix.ec_quality: Strong. Explains compensating controls for small businesses. Lists specific risks mitigated. Practical and scenario-grounded.
gap_matrix.choices_summary: A=ignoring the risk (obviously wrong), B=outsourcing with no oversight (removes control but doesn't remove responsibility), C=eliminating all internal controls (obviously wrong), D=increased owner review as compensating (correct). A and C are overtly bad advice.

gap_matrix.topic: Control environment — tone at the top
gap_matrix.subtopic: Board/executive integrity emphasis = COSO control environment
gap_matrix.ec_quality: Strong. Names control environment as COSO foundation. Explains tone at the top. Could add explicit COSO cube reference.
gap_matrix.choices_summary: A=monitoring, B=risk assessment, C=information and communication, D=control environment/tone at the top (correct). All three distractors are other COSO components. Correct answer mentions 'tone at the top' — giveaway for prepared candidates.

gap_matrix.subtopic: Susceptibility before considering controls = inherent risk
gap_matrix.ec_quality: Strong. Clearly distinguishes inherent risk from control risk. Teaches candidate to read stem for clues ('before controls'). Pedagogically effective.
gap_matrix.choices_summary: A=inherent risk (correct), B=detection risk, C=control risk (strongest distractor — common confusion), D=business risk. Stem says 'before considering controls' — gives away answer.

gap_matrix.topic: Segregation of duties — cash custody and recording
gap_matrix.subtopic: Custody + recordkeeping = concealment risk (classic SoD weakness)
gap_matrix.ec_quality: Adequate. Explains custody + recordkeeping = concealment. Lacks COSO control-activity reference and exam-trap guidance.
gap_matrix.cc_note: Agent C (metadata) says B; Agent D (content) says A. DL-016 shift.
gap_matrix.choices_summary: A=physical access control weakness only, B=lack of SoD between custody and recordkeeping (correct), C=IT general control deficiency only, D=overly strong control environment. A and C use 'only' qualifiers (obvious elimination). D is sarcastic/funny.
certification_blockers: Distractors weak — 'only' qualifiers cue elimination. DL-031 pattern.

gap_matrix.subtopic: Owner/action plan/target date = remediation tracking process
gap_matrix.ec_quality: Strong. Explains remediation tracking as managed corrective-action process with accountability. Names owner/action plan/target date elements.
gap_matrix.cc_note: Agent C (metadata) says D; Agent D (content) says C. DL-016 shift.
gap_matrix.choices_summary: A=external audit sign-off (no internal follow-up), B=control environment assessment (broad, not deficiency-specific), C=risk acceptance (tolerates permanently), D=remediation tracking (correct). Good topic — monitoring subprocess.

gap_matrix.subtopic: Operational mgmt / risk oversight / internal audit = three lines model
gap_matrix.ec_quality: Good. Names three lines, explains each layer's purpose. Missing explicit IIA reference.
gap_matrix.choices_summary: A=three lines model (correct), B=COSO ERM cube, C=fraud triangle, D=balanced scorecard. Stem explicitly describes the three lines. DL-031 definition-match. Distractors are all unrelated frameworks. Labeled Difficult but is Understand/Remember.
certification_blockers: DL-031 — should be Easy/1 not Difficult/4

gap_matrix.topic: Access control — principle of least privilege
gap_matrix.subtopic: Limiting access to job duties = least privilege security principle
gap_matrix.ec_quality: Good. Names least privilege, explains what it limits. Concise but missing real-world scenario connection.
gap_matrix.dl010_note: MEDIUM (S809.2): EWD text references 'limiting user access' which is unrelated to the question about independent verification. Cross-item contamination.
gap_matrix.choices_summary: A=risk transfer, B=principle of least privilege (correct), C=management override, D=principle of maximum access for efficiency (humorous/opposite). DL-031 definition-match. D is silly/funny — obviously wrong.
certification_blockers: DL-031 — should be Easy/1 not Difficult/4

gap_matrix.subtopic: Supervisor recount as detective independent verification control
gap_matrix.ec_quality: Good. Names independent verification, categorizes as detective. Clear distinction from SoD. Solid instructive value.
gap_matrix.choices_summary: A=physical control over inventory storage only, B=independent verification (correct), C=preventive control (stops errors before they occur), D=segregation of duties. Critical distinction between independent verification and SoD — common CMA confusion. Labeled Difficult but content is Understand.

gap_matrix.subtopic: Purchasing insurance = risk transfer/sharing response
gap_matrix.ec_quality: Definition-level. Correctly identifies insurance as risk transfer. Very brief — no contrast with other responses, no business context, no exam traps.
gap_matrix.dl013_detail: Both EW_B and EW_C contain generic template text: 'This option reflects a misunderstanding of erm risk response strategies...' No choice-specific educational value.
gap_matrix.choices_summary: A=risk appetite (definitional), B=risk avoidance (eliminates entirely), C=risk acceptance (no action), D=risk transfer (correct). All distractors are real ERM response strategies. Good choices ruined by boilerplate explanations.
certification_blockers: DL-013: EW_B and EW_C are boilerplate (9 slots affected across Pack D)

gap_matrix.subtopic: Manager PO approval = preventive authorization control
gap_matrix.ec_quality: Adequate. Names authorization control as preventive. Short — no exam-trap or COSO component mapping.
gap_matrix.choices_summary: A=authorization control (correct), B=monitoring activity (after the fact), C=segregation of duties only, D=risk assessment activity. Tests control activity vs. monitoring vs. risk assessment COSO component discrimination. Labeled Difficult but is Understand.

gap_matrix.subtopic: Periodic review of exceptions/recons = COSO monitoring component
gap_matrix.ec_quality: Good. Names monitoring as COSO component. Distinguishes ongoing evaluation from transaction-level controls. Clear evaluative vs. executional distinction.
gap_matrix.choices_summary: A=risk assessment, B=information and communication, C=control environment, D=monitoring activities (correct). All distractors are other COSO components. Monitoring vs. I&C is a real CMA trap. Appropriate difficulty calibration (Difficult/Apply).

gap_matrix.subtopic: Offsite backups + DR plan = availability control objective (CIA triad)
gap_matrix.ec_quality: Good. Names availability as control objective. Explains purpose of offsite backups and DR plans. Cleanly maps to CIA triad element.
gap_matrix.choices_summary: A=SoD within IT, B=authorization controls over transaction approval, C=availability of systems/data (correct), D=confidentiality only. Tests CIA triad distinction (availability vs. confidentiality). D is key distractor.

gap_matrix.subtopic: Testing/approval/documentation before production = ITGC change management
gap_matrix.ec_quality: WEAKEST EC in audit (score 3). Bare statement identifying change management as ITGC. No explanation of WHY testing/approval/documentation matter. Fails CAQS §4 mini-lesson standard.
gap_matrix.dl013_detail: Both EW_B and EW_C contain generic template boilerplate. Zero educational value. Good question ruined by bad explanations.
gap_matrix.choices_summary: A=SoD control unrelated to IT, B=application control embedded in transaction, C=physical control over hardware only, D=IT general control (correct). B tests key ITGC vs. application control distinction.
certification_blockers: EC critically low (score 3, 144 chars — no principle, no interpretation)

gap_matrix.subtopic: Likelihood × impact scoring = risk assessment process
gap_matrix.ec_quality: Good. Names risk assessment, explains likelihood-impact ranking methodology. Cleanly structured.

DL-031 definition-match. Stem says 'scores risks based on likelihood and impact' = answer is 'risk assessment'. Labeled Difficult but is Understand.

gap_matrix.subtopic: MFA reduces unauthorized access risk to financial systems

gap_matrix.subtopic: Declining costly control for low-frequency risk = cost-benefit limitation

All distractors are real risks in different cycles/domains. B tests revenue vs. disbursement cycle — good trap.

certification_blocker_analysis:
DL-026 is the universal certification blocker for all 38 Domain E seeds. Every single seed has at least 1 empty non-CorrectChoice ExplanationWrong slot — meaning learners who select specific wrong answers receive NO educational feedback. 53 of 114 total non-CC distractor slots (46.5%) are empty.

Secondary blockers (layered on top of DL-026):
- DL-013: 5 Pack D seeds have 9 boilerplate ExplanationWrong slots with generic template text ('This option reflects a misunderstanding...') that provide zero choice-specific educational value. These slots count as 'non-empty' structurally but are pedagogically useless.
- DL-010: 3 seeds (P1-EC-020, P1-ED-010, P1-ED-051) have ExplanationWrong text assigned to the wrong choice or describing an entirely different question's distractors. Learners see unrelated feedback.
- EC quality: 6 seeds (P1-EC-004, P1-EC-014, P1-EC-031, P1-ED-016, P1-ED-036, P1-ED-075) have ExplanationCorrect scores of 3-5 (definition-only or bare statements) — below the CAQS §4 mini-lesson standard.
- DL-031: ~12 seeds exhibit the definition-match pattern where the stem directly defines the correct answer, making the item trivially easy. These are labeled Moderate or Difficult but should be Easy(1).
- DL-016: 5 seeds have metadata-block vs. content-block CorrectChoice divergence. The content-block CC is authoritative for learner-facing content. EW slot remediation assignments depend on which CC is used as reference.
- Distractor quality: 3 seeds (P1-EC-008 DQS 14, P1-ED-010 DQS 19, P1-ED-051 DQS 21) have critically low distractor quality scores requiring redesign, not just EW authoring.

Certification readiness assessment: 0 of 38 seeds are certification-ready in current state. 23 seeds need only DL-026 fixes (1 empty slot each). 15 seeds need 2 DL-026 fixes. 5 seeds additionally need DL-013 boilerplate replacement. 3 seeds additionally need DL-010 correction. 5 seeds need CC audit before any EW work. Minimum viable certification path: fix the top 10 priority seeds first (ranks 1-10) — these are the strongest items needing the fewest changes (1 empty slot each + strong EC + good distractors) and would yield the highest certification ROI.

Per CAQS §1.7.2, certification requires: (1) HIGH-confidence AI verification across all 6 dimensions, (2) user approval documented in REVISION_HISTORY.md, (3) distractor tier map recorded, (4) zero low-confidence claims. With 53 empty EW slots, certification is blocked on ALL 38 seeds. The EW integrity audit confirms 0 DL-008 violations (all CC slots are correctly empty), so DL-008 is NOT a blocker.
